home.heroDesc: Verify once, encrypt and distribute, and enforce across decentralized nodes.
home.overviewBody1: DIDN provides a privacy-preserving verification workflow where data is verified once and reused securely.
home.overviewBody2: Encrypted shards are distributed across nodes to improve resilience and reduce single points of failure.
home.authorityBody1: A trusted authority verifies user attributes once (e.g., age or student status).
home.authorityBody2: The signed result can be reused without exposing raw personal data.
home.storageBody1: Verification artifacts are encrypted and split into shards for distributed storage.
home.storageBody2: Threshold reconstruction and integrity checks help maintain privacy and reliability.
home.requestCardBody: A verifier requests proof of a specific attribute without asking for the full identity.
home.executionCardBody: Nodes validate policies and cryptographic proofs against stored artifacts.
home.responseCardBody: The verifier receives a yes/no (or policy-compliant proof), not the underlying data.
home.trustBody1: The authority is trusted only for the initial verification step, not for ongoing access.
home.trustBody2: Decentralized nodes enforce policies, reduce single points of failure, and improve transparency.

about.title: About DIDN
about.body: DIDN is a course project that explores privacy-preserving verification using decentralized storage and threshold cryptography. Our goal is to let user data be verified once by a trusted authority, then encrypted and distributed across independent nodes—so future checks can return policy-compliant proofs without exposing raw personal data.
bullets: Reduce repeated identity verification and unnecessary data exposure
Minimize trust after the initial verification step

faqs.q: How does DIDN protect my personal data?
faqs.a: DIDN minimizes exposure by encrypting verification artifacts and distributing them across nodes. Only policy-compliant results are returned during checks.
A verifier asks for proof of an attribute (e.g., age over 18). The system returns a yes/no or policy-compliant proof without revealing raw data.

faqs.q: Why do I see Pending / History on my dashboard?
faqs.a: Pending items are requests awaiting action. History shows completed outcomes for your records.

faqs.q: I selected the wrong language. How do I change it?
faqs.a: Use the language selector in the top navigation. The selected language is kept in the URL parameter (?lang=...).
